notes: The E8 warning is not a real problem for this manual, so the graph is unchanged from my previous answer. The catalogue's 6.0-24 V supply range for the UNO R4 Minima applies to power fed into VIN or the 5V pin. Here the 5V pin is only an output: the red wire takes the board's regulated 5 V to the breadboard + rail for the potentiometer, as the circuit image shows. Nothing external is fed into the 5V pin.
The board is powered over USB, the same connection used to upload the sketch. I did not add a USB cable or other power source, because the tutorial's parts list and circuit image do not show one.
The parts are the same as in step 1. Nothing was added or dropped.
The image is the authority for the wiring. The yellow wire from A0 goes to the buzzer, and the yellow wire from A5 goes to the potentiometer wiper. A0 is the DAC output on the UNO R4 Minima.

The breadboard image labels its top half f-j and its bottom half a-e, but the catalogue calls the top bank 't' and the bottom bank 'b'. I used the catalogue's names, so image-top is 't' and image-bottom is 'b'. Only which holes share a strip matters.

The potentiometer straddles the centre gap. Its wiper (SIG) is in column 14 of the top bank. Its two outer legs are in columns 13 and 15 of the bottom bank. The red jumper in column 13 goes to the + rail, so that leg is VCC. The black jumper in column 15 goes to the - rail, so that leg is GND.

The buzzer legs sit in columns 26 and 30 of the bottom bank. The A0 wire lands in column 26, the signal side, so I used pin 2 (+) there. The black jumper in column 30 goes to the ground rail, so pin 1 (-) is there.
Rail hole numbers are estimated from the image. The bottom rail's upper row is the black-marked negative rail (bn) and its lower row is the red-marked positive rail (bp).
The buzzer is driven directly from the DAC pin with no series resistor, as in the tutorial image.
